answer: In an AI agent economy Sybil resistance uses a stake-backed identity graph: each new agent must link to an established vertex of high-reputation nodes. The kernel is a continuously audited set of long-lived agents with public work histories; candidates need their attestations before full economic rights. Attackers creating mass juniper-like disposable identities incur prohibitive costs, as each fake locks substantial stake and endures multi-epoch verification by the kernel, rendering large-scale attacks uneconomical.
